actions.description: Search the actions available to the current principal and MCP profile. An empty query (the default) returns everything visible, up to limit. Filter by effect to find only "read", "write", "destructive" and so on. Each result is a summary; pass its id to capabilities.describe for the full input and output schema.

Return the exact input schema, output schema and authorization policy for one action, by id. The natural second call after capabilities.search, when a summary is not enough to construct the arguments.

List recent durable action executions in the current workspace: the operations that run async rather than returning inline, in "claimed", "queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed" or "cancelled" status. Filter by actionId or status. Pass an id to operations.get for the full step-by-step detail.

Read one durable action operation by id, including its steps array (each with its own status and optional progress) and, once failed, an error object with a code, message and whether it is retryable. Poll this or use operations.wait to watch it settle.

Wait briefly for a durable operation to change or reach a terminal state, up to timeoutMs (0 to 30000, default 10000). Returns as soon as the operation moves, or once the timeout elapses, whichever comes first. Returns the same shape as operations.get either way.

Request cancellation of a cancellable operation. This is a request, not a guarantee: an operation past its cancellable point keeps running. Requires speko:execute, unlike the speko:read reads in this group. Check operations.get or operations.wait afterward to see whether it actually reached "cancelled".

List OAuth client grants and product API keys for the current workspace control plane. oauthGrants carry the scopes each connected client holds; apiKeys carry a revoked flag and lastUsedAt (null if never used). Pass an oauthGrants id to agent_access.oauth_grant.revoke to remove one. OAuth-user principals only.

Revoke one OAuth client grant for the current user and workspace. consentId is the id field from agent_access.overview's oauthGrants array, not the client id. Requires speko:credentials, a scope not used elsewhere on this surface.

Get the current workspace and its capability flags: features.buyPhoneNumbers, sms10dlc, smsMessaging, imessageIntegration, agentDuplication and others, each as an {enabled} object. retrievalProvider and imessageProvider are null when the corresponding integration is not configured.
Get the current workspace prepaid credit balance in USD, as of updatedAt. Requires the speko:billing scope, unlike most reads on this surface.

List recent credit movements for the current workspace, newest first. Filter with kind as a comma-separated list of "grant", "debit", "topup", "refund" and "adjustment". Page with the returned nextCursor; it is null on the last page. provider, sessionId and stripePaymentIntentId are populated only on the entry kinds that produced them.

Get workspace usage, managed cost and current balance. from_ and to bound the window; omit both for all-time. breakdown lists cost per provider and metric, with keySource "BYOK" or "MANAGED" showing whether the workspace supplied its own provider key for that line.

List product API keys in the current workspace, each with its scopes, revocation state, and resourceVersion. resourceVersion is literally "active" or "revoked", not an incrementing version, so it stays valid for api_keys.revoke as long as the key remains active; there is no need to re-read it immediately before revoking.

Create a product API key and return its secret in `key` exactly once; it is never retrievable again, so store it immediately. `scopes` is 1 to 6 values from speko:read, write, execute, billing, credentials, compliance, and the key can only do what those scopes allow. `routing_policy`, if set, pins this key to a specific stt/llm/tts provider chain and objective instead of the workspace default; omit it to inherit the default. Available to any workspace member, unlike other credential actions on this surface which require an admin.

Revoke one product API key. `expected_resource_version` must be "active", the only value an unrevoked key ever has; it does not need a fresh read from api_keys.list first, since the value cannot go stale while the key stays active. Concurrent revokes are safe: only one succeeds, the other is refused. Revocation cannot be undone.

Get one snapshot of the current workspace Gateway: session counts (total, last 24h, active), 24h error count, active key count, workload and instance counts, and settled spend in micros. Each figure has its own detail action when the summary number is not enough: gateway.workloads.list, gateway.instances.list, gateway.activity.list, gateway.usage.get.
List Gateway workloads in the current workspace, each identified by type and id, with its total and active session counts and when it was last seen.

List Gateway runtime instances in the current workspace, each with its active and pending session counts, capacity, and whether it is online, draining, or already offline. `draining: true` means the instance is finishing its current sessions and refusing new ones ahead of a planned shutdown. `offlineAt` is null while online and set once it drops off.

List recent Gateway activity events for the current workspace, newest first, optionally filtered to one workload, one instance, or one event_type. Each row carries the provider and session/attempt ids. `attribution`, when present, names which client made the request under a fixed evidence classification. A malformed attribution on an otherwise-valid event silently drops to undefined rather than failing the row, so an absent attribution does not mean the event is invalid.

Get aggregated Gateway usage for the current workspace, broken down by provider: spend in micros of the given currency, session count, and the metering source behind the number when more than one exists.

List legacy Runtime API keys still valid during the migration window, each with its expiry, revocation state, and resourceVersion. `legacyAcceptUntil`, when present, is the workspace-level deprecation cutoff date for these keys, set by the Runtime service rather than this action. gateway.legacy_keys.revoke needs the resourceVersion from this list as a concurrency token.

Revoke one legacy Runtime API key. `expected_resource_version` must match the key's current resourceVersion from gateway.legacy_keys.list; a stale value is refused rather than revoking blind, so read the key immediately before revoking. Revocation cannot be undone.

List Relay models with their provider, kind (stt, tts, llm, s2s, or evaluation), routability, and benchmark and ranking data for the given objective and language. Filtering by `language` narrows to models that actually serve it; omit both filters to see the full catalog and every language it covers. gateway.relay.tts_preview.create and other Relay-routed actions expect a (provider, model, voice) combination taken from this list, not guessed.

List recent Relay requests, newest first, each with its full attempt chain: every provider tried, in order, with an outcome of served, failed, or superseded. `superseded` marks an attempt that a later, faster attempt beat rather than one that errored, so counting it as a failure overstates the failover rate. `routing_mode` is auto when Relay chose the chain and explicit when the caller pinned it.

Get Relay usage summed over a bounded recent window (1 to 2160 hours, default 168, one week), with total requests, failures, and failovers, the same three broken out as a time series, and again split by kind and by model. Failures and failovers are reported as separate counters, not combined into one rate.

Get the Runtime credit snapshot Relay uses to admit new requests: available balance in micros, open reserved micros not yet settled, and unexported settled micros not yet reflected in the platform balance. `source` is "platform" when the balance comes from the platform ledger and "runtime_default" when Runtime is using its own fallback figure instead.

List Relay provider credentials for the current workspace without exposing stored key values; only the last four characters, if configured, are shown. `resource_version`, present when configured, is the concurrency token gateway.provider_credentials.replace and .delete require.

Create a Relay provider credential, or replace the existing one for that provider. `expected_resource_version` defaults to null, meaning no credential is expected to exist yet; set it to the current resource_version from gateway.provider_credentials.list to replace one that does, and the request is refused if the stored value has moved on since. The submitted `api_key` is never echoed back; only its last four characters appear afterward in gateway.provider_credentials.list.

Delete a Relay provider credential. `expected_resource_version` must match the current resource_version from gateway.provider_credentials.list; a stale value is refused rather than deleting blind, so read the credential immediately before deleting rather than reusing an earlier version.

List recent Gateway profiler conversations, each with its turn counts (total, evaluated, good) and good_turn_rate when evaluation has run, plus how it ended: hangup, transfer, error, shutdown, or unknown. gateway.profiler.conversations.get returns one conversation's full turn-by-turn detail; gateway.profiler.turn_trace.get goes one level deeper into a single turn.

Get one profiler conversation with every turn assembled: latency breakdown (ear-to-mouth, endpointing, LLM time to first token, tool time, TTS time to first audio), barge-in and overspeech timing, and a `confidence` of complete, degraded, or minimal reflecting how many of the expected markers actually arrived. `violations` and `missing_markers` name specifics when confidence is not complete. gateway.profiler.turn_trace.get returns the raw event trace behind one turn when this summary is not enough.

Get the raw, ordered event trace behind one profiler turn: every marker event with its type, sequence number, and millisecond timestamp, alongside the same turn summary gateway.profiler.conversations.get already returns. Use this when a turn's `confidence` is degraded or minimal and the summary alone does not explain which marker was missing or out of order.

Create a bounded Relay TTS preview and return a short-lived audio resource link. The voice id is not cross-checked against the chosen provider before synthesis. An id that belongs to a different vendor (for example an OpenAI voice name passed with provider: "azure") can be accepted and still fail or return silence instead of erroring up front. See gateway.models.list for a language's available provider and model pairs; prefer a voice already listed under the chosen provider.

List agents in the current workspace without their full system prompts. Each item includes voice, turnHandling and runMode as currently stored. Use agents.get for one agent when the full system prompt is also needed.

Get one agent and its complete editable configuration, including voice, turnHandling (profile, dtmfToolDescription, amdPrompt) and system prompt. Read this before diagnosing a silent call or a missing keypad response. Voice is not validated against what the TTS provider owns. The keypad tool only arms when turnHandling.profile is "ivr" or AMD detects a machine mid-call.

Duplicate an agent and its copyable tools, knowledge, evaluations, version, and graph. The copy carries the source voice and turnHandling settings forward unchanged. Check the returned warnings array. TOOL_AUTH_REQUIRED means a copied tool is registered on the new agent but needs its credentials or auth headers reconnected, so a duplicated agent can show a tool as present while it silently fails until that happens. WEBHOOK_AUTH_REQUIRED is a separate case: it applies to lifecycle webhooks (preCall, postCall, status, analysis, recording), not tools, and those are copied already disabled rather than left silently broken, so each one needs its auth fixed and then re-enabled by hand. INTEGRATION_DISCONNECTED and GRAPH_NOT_COPIED name the other two things that did not carry over.

Create an AI phone receptionist for a small business in one step, without deploying it. Reads the business website when website_url is given (public http/https pages only; a page that cannot be read is reported in website.status = "failed" and setup still completes from the notes). Builds the system prompt from mode and the facts, a short greeting that says it is an AI (and that the call is recorded when recording is on for the workspace), and a transfer to owner_phone; emergency_escalation also escalates to backup_phone when the owner does not answer. No knowledge base or search tool is created when there are no facts. Returns the new agent id, a preview of exactly what it will say and will never do, and missingFacts: the questions to ask the owner, whose answers go to receptionist.update_facts. The agent is NOT live: next call agents.test_call to ring the owner, then receptionist.go_live. Repeating a call with the same idempotency key returns the first result instead of creating a second receptionist. Errors: RECEPTIONIST_RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED (receptionists are not available on the call runtime of this workspace yet; nothing was created, contact support).

Correct or add business facts on a receptionist made by receptionist.setup, in plain text (for example "we close at 6 on Fridays, a haircut is $40"). The correction is applied to the stored facts, the prompt and greeting are rebuilt, and the same preview shape as setup is returned so the owner can check it again. Corrections are kept in order and the newest wins when two disagree. Returns RECEPTIONIST_NOT_FOUND (404) for an agent that was not made by receptionist.setup in this workspace. Does not deploy.

Read the authored execution graph stored for one agent version. Omit `version` for the agent latest. Returns graph:null when the version has no graph yet (not an error). Read this before agents.graph.replace so an edit starts from the current graph, never a guess.

entryNodeId.description: Id of the single `entry`-kind node the walk starts at.

globalEdges.description: Intents a caller may raise from any node. Send them back or they are dropped.

kind.description: Node kind. The worker walks entry / message / tool / note / transfer / end today; the others are authorable and saved, and the response names any the runtime cannot walk yet.

instruction.description: What the model should accomplish at this node.

say.description: A verbatim line. End nodes speak this exactly.

key.description: State key, a slug ([A-Za-z0-9_]+). Expression edges reference it.

edgeOrder.description: Edge ids in the order this node evaluates its branches.

digitSlot.description: `press_digit`: state key ([A-Za-z0-9_]+) the pressed digit lands in.

code.description: `code`: expression evaluated over the state store.

mustBeHeard.description: The say line must be HEARD before the walk leaves by this node's own edges. When the worker gives up on it (talked over past the re-read cap, or never delivered twice) it goes to `unheardFallback` instead of treating the line as asked.

unheardFallback.description: `mustBeHeard`: node id the walk goes to when the line is never heard.

answerLength.description: `message`: how long an answer the step expects. `open` keeps AssemblyAI waiting through pauses (turn silence min 1300 / max 3600 ms); `short` keeps the agent STT settings so yes/no replies stay fast. Unset: a free-text slot -> open, choice-only slots -> short.

position.description: Authored canvas placement. Preserve it on a write or the layout is re-derived.

actions.description: Publish an authored execution graph as a NEW agent version. A graph change is a change to the agent, so it cuts a version the same way a config change does: the live config is carried forward unchanged and only the graph differs, which is what makes agents.rollback able to restore a previous workflow. WHOLE-OBJECT REPLACE — the graph you send becomes the graph, so read agents.graph.get first and send the full modified object, never a partial patch. Marks the graph source as "authored", which permanently protects it from the seeder. Rejects with INVALID_GRAPH plus the exact per-field reasons when the graph fails structural validation, and with VERSION_CONFLICT when a precondition failed — the message says whether the agent was published since you read it, the version you sent is not the live one, or the graph itself changed under you. Re-read with agents.graph.get and retry rather than forcing. A graph that saves can still come back with `warnings` (code GRAPH_LINT): legal shapes the validator flags, each naming the node, the edge and the fix. The graph IS saved; read them and replace again if the fix applies.

version.description: Required. The version you EDITED FROM — the one agents.graph.get returned. Used as a concurrency token: if it is no longer the live version the write is refused rather than burying whoever published in between. The graph lands on a new version.

actions.description: Derive a first execution graph for an agent version from its system prompt (falling back to the version derived flow). Idempotent: an existing graph is returned unchanged with status "exists". `force` re-derives ONLY over a previously seeded graph — an authored or healed graph is never clobbered. Use this to bootstrap, then agents.graph.replace to edit. `warnings` carries GRAPH_STALL_RISK when a fresh seed can hang, and GRAPH_LINT for validator findings on the graph returned, fresh or existing.

force.description: Re-derive over a stale `seeded` graph. Never overwrites `authored`/`healed`.

actions.description: Partially update one test case. Only the fields you send are written; omitted fields are left untouched. `description` and `source_call_id` accept null to clear them. Sending `input_payload` replaces it wholesale, so read the case first if you mean to keep its other keys — to change only the caller character use agents.evals.character.set instead.

Set or clear JUST the simulated-caller character on one test case. Merged into the existing input_payload without touching its other keys — this is the safe way to change a persona. Pass null to clear it back to a clean caller.
Delete one test case. Historical runs survive — the run rows reference the case through a nullable column, so the track record is not destroyed with the case.
The five most recent runs of ONE test case, newest first, each with the verdict in its result. Poll this after agents.evals.run to watch a case settle.

Author test cases for an agent from its own configuration — system prompt, intent, tools, knowledge-base titles and first message — using the scenario generator. Returns the generated cases WITHOUT saving by default; pass persist:true to also insert them as test cases. Calls an LLM, so it is slower than the other actions here.

persist.description: Insert the generated cases as test cases instead of only returning them.

actions.description: Pass-rate over time for one agent, as a contiguous zero-filled series plus window totals. Manual test calls are excluded — they are hardcoded-pass and would inflate the rate. Out-of-range `days` clamps rather than erroring.

bucket.description: UTC date key for the bucket start, YYYY-MM-DD.

actions.description: Ask for a minimal system-prompt revision that would make a FAILED run pass. The failures are extracted from the run itself, so you only need the run id. Read-only — it proposes, it does not deploy; pass the result to agents.apply_prompt_fix to ship it. Returns status "no_fix_needed" when the run has no failures.

Ask for a minimal system-prompt revision from failures you supply yourself, when the failures did not come from one stored run. Prefer agents.evals.runs.suggest_fix when you have a run id. Read-only — it proposes, it does not deploy.

Deploy a revised system prompt as a NEW agent version. Takes the current live config, swaps the prompt, and deploys — which auto-enqueues a version-stamped re-test, closing the fail → suggest → apply → re-test loop. Send the FULL prompt, not a diff. Requires the agent to already have a deployed version.

based_on_run.description: The run this fix answers — recorded in the new version source.

actions.description: Re-pin ONE pipeline layer (stt, llm or tts) to a different provider and deploy that as a new agent version — the fix that is not a prompt change. Every other layer and config key is carried forward. Auto-enqueues a re-test like agents.apply_prompt_fix.

Read the agent's LIVE system prompt back as a structured decision view — its goals, the rules it follows, and its conditional branches, plus a best-effort flow. Derived on demand, not stored. Returns status "empty" when the agent has no prompt yet.
List the organization scenario library, newest first. A scenario is one thing a caller is trying to do, reusable across agents. Pass `agent_id` to list only the scenarios attached to that agent.

Author a scenario into the organization library and optionally attach it to agents. Deduped by content: an identical scenario already in the org (for example one the reliability gate derived) is reused and only the attachments are added, so re-running this never creates a twin. Scenario content is FROZEN at creation — there is no update action by design; evolve a scenario by creating a new one and calling scenarios.archive on the old one with superseded_by.

job.description: The task the caller is trying to complete.

success_criteria.description: The bar the agent must clear for this scenario to count as passed.

actions.description: Attach a library scenario to an agent so the reliability gate drives it there. Supply `persona_id` to pin the caller character this agent runs the scenario with (persona x scenario compose); pass null to clear it; omit it to leave an existing pin unchanged.
Detach a library scenario from one agent. The scenario itself and its history survive — only the agent link is removed.

Archive a scenario — the only lifecycle transition there is. An archived scenario stops being driven by the gate but keeps its run history. Pass `superseded_by` with the id of the scenario that replaces it to record the lineage; the replacement must already exist in this organization and cannot be the scenario itself.

List up to 50 recent reliability runs that exercised this scenario, each with the per-scenario verdict it produced — the scenario track record across agent versions. Only runs written after the gate began stamping scenarioId carry the link, so older runs will not appear.

Create a short-lived Stripe Checkout handoff for adding workspace credits. Returns a url, its purpose, and an expiresAt timestamp; the caller opens the url to complete payment, this action does not itself move any money. amount_usd is a whole dollar figure between 5 and 10,000. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

Create a short-lived Stripe Billing Portal handoff for the workspace. Returns a url, its purpose, and an expiresAt timestamp; the portal itself lets the account owner manage payment methods and view invoices on Stripe. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

Create a short-lived Stripe handoff for authorizing an auto-top-up card. Returns a url, its purpose, and an expiresAt timestamp; completing it on Stripe attaches a payment method without itself enabling auto-top-up. Call billing.auto_topup.update afterward with enabled true plus a threshold and amount to turn charging on. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

Create a short-lived Stripe Checkout handoff that subscribes the workspace to a flat monthly plan (muse_starter). Each paid month adds the plan's included credit to the balance. Returns a url, its purpose, and an expiresAt timestamp; the caller opens the url to pay, this action moves no money itself. Fails with PLAN_NOT_CONFIGURED when the plan is not on sale and PLAN_ALREADY_ACTIVE when the workspace already subscribes. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

List recent Stripe invoices for the current workspace, newest first. limit caps the page size at 100 and defaults to 25. Each invoice reports amountPaid and amountDue in the smallest currency unit, plus nullable hostedInvoiceUrl and invoicePdf links once Stripe has generated them.

Get the current automatic credit top-up configuration and payment-method status. hasPaymentMethod and the nested paymentMethod fields cover the card Stripe has on file, separate from whether auto-top-up is enabled. A nonzero failureCount with pausedAt and lastFailureReason set means a top-up attempt failed and charging is paused. Call billing.auto_topup.resume to clear that once the underlying issue is fixed, or billing.auto_topup.update to reconfigure a new threshold or amount.

Replace the automatic credit top-up configuration for the workspace. This is a whole-object replace, not a patch. enabled, thresholdCents, and amountCents must all be sent together even to change only one of them, and thresholdCents must be strictly less than amountCents or the call is rejected. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

Clear a paused auto-top-up failure state so charging may resume, without changing the threshold or amount on file. Check billing.auto_topup.get first to confirm pausedAt is actually set; calling this when auto-top-up was never paused is a no-op. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

Get the workspace monthly spending cap and how much of it this month has used. monthlyCapUsd is null when no cap is set. While reached is true, new sessions, outbound calls and test calls are refused with SPENDING_CAP_REACHED and inbound calls go unanswered instead of being charged; calls already in progress are not cut. Spend is managed usage charged in the current UTC calendar month and resets at resetsAt.

Set the workspace monthly spending cap in whole US dollars (1 to 100,000), or null to remove it. Takes effect immediately: if this month has already spent the new cap, new sessions and calls stop until the month resets or the cap is raised. Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

List the integrations this workspace can use (calendars, CRMs) with each one's connected installations. connectable is true when integrations.connect can start an OAuth connection for the app; tool_modes lists the modes agents.integration_tools.attach accepts for it. An app with an empty installations array is not connected yet. Installation status "disconnected" or "error" means the owner has to connect it again before an agent can use it. On the Muse surface only Google Calendar and HighLevel are listed.

Start connecting an OAuth integration (e.g. Google Calendar, HighLevel). Returns a short-lived url (ten minutes, single use) to a Speko page that names this workspace and asks the account owner to confirm; Continue takes them to the provider to sign in and grant access, Cancel ends the link. Nothing is connected until they finish there. The browser does not need a Speko session. Give the url only to the owner of this workspace. Afterwards integrations.list shows the new installation, and agents.integration_tools.attach gives an agent its tools. Errors: INTEGRATION_APP_NOT_FOUND (unknown or not offered on this surface), INTEGRATION_NOT_OAUTH (configured in the dashboard instead), OAUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED (this deployment cannot connect the app). Requires a human OAuth principal, not an API key.

app_key.description: Integration app key from integrations.list, e.g. "google_calendar" or "leadconnector".

actions.description: Give an agent the tools of a connected integration installation. Replaces that app's integration tools on the agent with the set for mode, so calling it again switches modes cleanly; other tools are untouched. Modes: availability_only (only checks free times, books nothing; the owner confirms every booking), booking_requests (auto-booking: the agent checks availability and creates new appointments by itself; HighLevel also creates a new contact for the caller and logs a note; it never looks up, edits or cancels an existing contact or appointment), all_actions (every action the app offers, with no booking guardrails). The default is availability_only where the app supports it; use booking_requests only when the owner explicitly asks the agent to book by itself. Booking tools are described so the agent checks availability before offering any time and never invents one; guardrail_prompt is the matching system-prompt section. For a receptionist (receptionist.setup) the agent's instructions are rebuilt to match the new tools and instructions_updated is true; detach rebuilds them again. calendar_id pins which calendar the tools use: optional for Google (defaults to the primary calendar), required for HighLevel booking modes unless the sub-account has exactly one calendar, in which case it is picked automatically; CALENDAR_CHOICE_REQUIRED lists the choices. pipeline_id (and optional pipeline_stage_id) adds HighLevel opportunity creation. Changes apply to the next call. Errors: AGENT_NOT_FOUND, INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND, INTEGRATION_DISCONNECTED (connect it again with integrations.connect), INTEGRATION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED, CALENDAR_CHOICE_REQUIRED, TOOL_NAME_TAKEN (the agent already has a non-integration tool with the same name), RECEPTIONIST_UPDATE_FAILED (tools changed but the receptionist's instructions did not; call again), CALENDAR_ALREADY_ATTACHED (a receptionist uses one calendar app; detach the current one first).

instructions_updated.description: True when the agent is a receptionist and its instructions were rebuilt to match these tools; guardrail_prompt is then already part of them.

actions.description: Remove an integration app's tools from an agent (only tools of kind integration for that app; webhook and other tools are never touched). The installation stays connected for other agents. Returns the removed tool names; an empty list means the agent had none. Changes apply to the next call.

app_key.description: Integration app key from integrations.list, e.g. "google_calendar" or "leadconnector".

actions.description: List phone and SIP numbers owned by the current workspace. For OAuth connectors, the first outbound call automatically provisions a dedicated number from workspace credits when none exists. Manual dashboard/API users keep the explicit declaration and purchase flow.

Get one phone or SIP number owned by the current workspace. setupStatus.status is "ready" only when inboundReady, outboundReady and agentReady are all true; check the setupStatus.issues array for what is still missing. A number can also carry suspendedAt with a suspensionReason of "billing" or "compliance", which blocks calls independently of setupStatus. Use phone_numbers.list to find a number id first.

Read this workspace's phone compliance status. OAuth connector workspaces submit automatically from the phone authorization accepted during sign-in; do not collect or submit declaration fields in chat. `submissionMode` identifies automatic OAuth, manual dashboard/API, or grandfathered migration handling.

Put an agent live as the business’s phone receptionist in one call: get a number (buy a new US/Canadian number, optionally by area code, or reuse one the workspace owns), link the agent to it for inbound calls in the same database write, enable outbound calling from it, deploy the agent, and return carrier-specific call-forwarding codes plus the exact codes that undo them. A purchased number always has the agent attached; there is no state in which it exists without one. Buying a number charges workspace credits (setup plus the first month). status "action_required" means nothing was bought or changed and requiredAction says what the owner must do: PHONE_NUMBER_KYB_REQUIRED / _ATTESTATION_REQUIRED / _REJECTED / _REVOKED / _REVIEW_HOLD (business verification, with a link), BUY_PHONE_NUMBERS_DISABLED_FOR_ORG, or INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE (add credits with billing.checkout.create, then call again). Errors: AGENT_NOT_FOUND, AGENT_ALREADY_HAS_NUMBER (the agent already answers another number; pass that number as phone_number_id), PHONE_NUMBER_IN_USE (the chosen number answers to another agent or a person), NO_NUMBERS_AVAILABLE (try another area code), DEPLOY_BLOCKED, KEPT_NUMBER_IN_USE (the kept number of a paused receptionist now answers another agent or a person; pass a number explicitly), RECEPTIONIST_RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED (receptionists are not available on the call runtime of this workspace yet; nothing was bought or deployed). Next: receptionist.verify_forwarding once the owner has dialed the forwarding code.

__schema3.description: Workspace number to use when number_source is "existing".

__schema7.description: Preferred 3-digit area code for a new number.

__schema9.description: A specific available number from phone_numbers.available.search.

__schema11.description: "overflow" (default): the business phone rings first and only missed or busy calls reach the receptionist. "all": every call goes to the receptionist.

__schema12.description: The owner’s existing business number that will forward to the receptionist.

__schema13.description: Carrier of the owner’s existing business line. "other" returns generic codes.

__schema14.description: Whether the business number is a mobile phone or a desk/office line.

__schema15.description: Email that receives a summary after every call. null turns email off.

__schema17.description: Mobile number for text summaries. Texts are sent only when the receptionist number is already registered for SMS and this number has opted in; email is always the primary channel. null turns texts off.

__schema19.description: When true, summaries contain only a secure sign-in link to the call, never the caller’s name, number or reason.

__schema21.description: Record this receptionist’s calls. false turns recording off for this agent; null follows the workspace setting. It cannot turn recording on when the workspace has recording off. When recording is on, the greeting must tell callers the call may be recorded.

actions.description: Check that calls to the owner’s business number actually reach the receptionist. Speko cannot place a test call into a carrier’s forwarding, so this is a two-step check: the first call (or restart: true) opens a 15-minute check window and returns status "waiting_for_test_call" with what the owner should do — call the business number from a DIFFERENT phone and, in overflow mode, let it ring out. Calling again reports what arrived on the receptionist number since the window opened: "verified" (a forwarded call reached the agent; evidence.forwardedFrom matches the business number), "probably_verified" (a call reached the agent but the carrier did not say it was forwarded), or "not_seen" (nothing yet; check the forwarding code or wait for the rings to run out). Errors: RECEPTIONIST_NOT_FOUND (run receptionist.go_live first), OWNER_NUMBER_REQUIRED (set owner_business_number via receptionist.settings.update).

Instant off switch: the receptionist stops answering its number right away. The number is kept (and still billed monthly) so receptionist.resume brings it back exactly as it was. While paused, calls that reach the Speko number are not answered, so the owner should also undo carrier forwarding (the returned undoForwarding) if callers should only ring the business phone. Safe to repeat.

Turn a paused receptionist back on: re-links the agent to its kept number so it answers again. Safe to repeat. Errors: RECEPTIONIST_NOT_FOUND, PHONE_NUMBER_IN_USE (someone linked the number to another agent or a person while paused), PHONE_NUMBER_GONE (the number was released; run receptionist.go_live).

Change a receptionist’s owner settings: who gets the post-call summary (email, text), privacy mode (link only, no caller details), per-agent recording, and the owner’s business line and forwarding mode. Partial update: omitted fields keep their value; null clears. Returns the settings and, when a business line is known, fresh forwarding codes. Errors: RECEPTIONIST_NOT_FOUND.

forwarding_mode.description: "overflow" (default): the business phone rings first and only missed or busy calls reach the receptionist. "all": every call goes to the receptionist.

owner_business_number.description: The owner’s existing business number that will forward to the receptionist.

owner_carrier.description: Carrier of the owner’s existing business line. "other" returns generic codes.

owner_line_type.description: Whether the business number is a mobile phone or a desk/office line.

notify_email.description: Email that receives a summary after every call. null turns email off.

notify_sms_number.description: Mobile number for text summaries. Texts are sent only when the receptionist number is already registered for SMS and this number has opted in; email is always the primary channel. null turns texts off.

notify_privacy_mode.description: When true, summaries contain only a secure sign-in link to the call, never the caller’s name, number or reason.

recording_enabled.description: Record this receptionist’s calls. false turns recording off for this agent; null follows the workspace setting. It cannot turn recording on when the workspace has recording off. When recording is on, the greeting must tell callers the call may be recorded.

actions.description: Cancel the receptionist so the owner stops paying for it, in one approval: it stops answering, the number go_live bought for it is released (which ends the monthly number charge; a released number cannot be recovered), and the result says how to undo carrier forwarding on the business phone. The agent itself is kept; delete it with agents.delete if it is no longer wanted. A monthly plan is not cancelled here: use billing.portal.create for that. A number the owner brought (an existing workspace number or an imported number), or one given to another agent or a person while paused, is never released: it is only unlinked and reported in keptNumber. Errors: NOT_FOUND (no receptionist for this agent), PHONE_NUMBER_RELEASE_FAILED (the number could not be released; nothing was charged and the receptionist stays paused, so retry).

Read this workspace's static-IP SIP gateway setup: connection details (gateway IP, SIP domain/realm, ports), the SIP login username and auth mode (never its password), the numbers routed through the gateway, numbers awaiting ownership verification by a test call, and the PBX outbound calls from gateway numbers go through (host, port, login; never its password). Requires SIP gateway access on the workspace. Logins and numbers are managed only in the dashboard; the outbound PBX only by Speko staff.

List visible knowledge bases, optionally filtered to one agent with agent_id. Each entry carries documentCount and chunkCount as current totals, not a snapshot from creation. Use knowledge_bases.documents.list on a specific base to see why those counts are what they are.
Get one knowledge base owned by the current workspace, including its embeddingModel and current documentCount and chunkCount. Use knowledge_bases.list to find a base id first.

List documents in a workspace knowledge base, each with an ingestion status of "pending", "processing", "ready" or "failed", and its own chunkCount. Use knowledge_bases.documents.get on a "failed" entry to read its errorMessage.

Get one document from a workspace knowledge base. status is one of "pending", "processing", "ready" or "failed"; errorMessage is set on "failed" and ingestedAt stays null until the document reaches "ready". Use knowledge_bases.documents.list to find a document id first.

Get the ordered transcript and per-turn latency for a workspace session, including any tool calls made mid-call (toolCalls, by name and args) and a latencyStatus per turn ("partial"|"complete"|"interrupted"|"error"). Use this to confirm whether a keypad press (send_dtmf) was invoked, or whether a turn with no agent text and an "error" latency status points to a synthesis failure rather than the callee hanging up.

Immediately request hang-up of a live voice or outbound phone session in this workspace. Use this when a call is stuck, no longer useful, or the user asks to stop it. Safe to repeat. Status ending means hang-up was requested; check sessions.get to confirm the session ended. Already ended sessions return already_ended.

session_id.description: The session ID returned when dialing.

actions.description: Open a support ticket with the Speko team on behalf of the signed-in user. summary is one line (3-200 characters); details is the full description (up to 4,000 characters). category is billing, calls, setup or other (default other). related optionally carries ids the team should look at: sessionId, callId, agentId, phoneNumber. Ids only: recordings and transcripts are never attached. Returns ticketId and expectedResponse; the user also receives a confirmation email and the team replies to that email address. Returns 429 SUPPORT_TICKET_RATE_LIMITED after too many tickets in a short time; the error says when to retry. A ticket is stored even when the team notification is delayed, so a success never needs a resend.
